text: The trip needs twenty-two thousand, three hundred kilograms of fuel. To turn litres into weight, you multiply by the fuel's density. They used one point seven seven. But that's pounds per litre, not kilograms. The right number was about zero point eight, so every litre was counted as more than twice its real weight. Every number on the sheet looked right. But the tanks held less than half the fuel the flight needed. At a stop in Ottawa, they dip the tanks again, and make the same mistake again. And with the gauges dead, nothing in the cockpit can warn them.
